Source depends on browser/router/web-UI-only modules with no native parity surface (rules 4/7), so a native-safe implementation was built importing NO DOM elements, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, or web UI components. The full behaviour contract (collapse/expand, active-section auto-expand, the filter-token matcher and filtered/expanded section derivation, the borrowed section glyph, the three trailing badges, pin/unpin, and the empty-filter clear affordance) is preserved and functional — it is not a render-nothing stub.

react-router-dom: useLocation has no DOM location on native, so effectivePath = pathname ?? '' and the host-supplied `pathname` prop is authoritative (the web Layout already passes it). <GuardedNavLink> (SPA navigation + dirty-form guard) maps to a <Pressable accessibilityRole="link"> that fires the existing onItemSelect callback (the web onClick={onSelect}, used by mobile to close the drawer); the destination `to` is preserved on the prop contract and exposed via accessibilityValue={{text: to}} so the host shell can wire route changes through the same data. aria-current -> accessibilityState={{selected}}.

react-i18next: useTranslation -> a local fallback hook returning a `t` that resolves to the inline English copy and interpolates {{token}} params, supporting BOTH call shapes the source uses — t(key, 'fallback') and t(key, { count|page, defaultValue }). All i18n keys are referenced verbatim: nav.sidebar, nav.favorites, nav.pages, nav.vehicleCount, nav.staleCount, nav.pinPage, nav.unpinPage, nav.filterNoMatch, nav.filterClear. i18next count-pluralization collapses to the {{count}} default string (documented).

@/lib/icons: item/section glyphs render from the passed-in icon component, now typed as a native SidebarIcon = React.ComponentType<{color?,size?}> (re-derived alongside the data contract). The internal lucide glyphs become native text/View stand-ins — Icons.next (ChevronRight) -> a '\u203a' caret rotated 90deg when expanded; Icons.star (pin) -> '\u2606'; Icons.close (unpin) -> '\u00d7'; Icons.home fallback -> a small drawn DefaultGlyph square. h-3.5/h-3 sizes map to 14/12.

@/components/ui Button variant=ghost size=sm -> a native IconGhostButton (Pressable) keeping the accessible pin/unpin label and press behaviour (e.preventDefault is unnecessary because the action is a sibling Pressable, not nested in the link). @/lib/cn Tailwind merging -> StyleSheet arrays. The group-hover reveal of pin/unpin collapses to always-visible because a touch device has no hover (matches web-on-touch). CSS-var/Tailwind visual intent maps to theme tokens: --text-primary/secondary/muted -> colors.textPrimary/textSecondary/textMuted; --theme-primary -> colors.accent (notification dot, clear-filter text); bg-white/[0.05] active + bg-white/[0.03] hover -> rgba literals on the row pressed/active styles; h-7 -> minHeight 28; ps-2/ps-7 -> paddingStart 8/28; text-[13px]/[11px]/[10px]/[12px] -> matching fontSize. data-role -> testID='notion-sidebar'; data-tour -> per-row testID; data-testid='notion-sidebar-empty-filter' -> testID; role='status' -> accessibilityLiveRegion='polite'.

./LinearSidebar shared types (LinearSidebarSectionInput/LinearSidebarProps) are re-derived locally because the native LinearSidebar has not been ported yet, then re-exported under the Notion names (NotionSidebarSectionInput, NotionSidebarProps) plus SidebarIcon/SidebarIconProps so the data contract stays identical to the web. The vestigial `filter` state (only ever cleared via the Clear-filter button in this Notion variant, never set to a non-empty value) is ported verbatim to keep faithful behaviour.
